result:
None of the three solutions is clearly right, so my pick is a low-confidence guess.

**Solution 1** claims the ratio is 1. It overlooks the diamond operators coming from the p-part of $(A/\wp^r)^\times$. That part has order $q^{D(r-1)}$. In characteristic $p$, a $p$-power-order character is trivial, so these characters collapse and the diamond action becomes unipotent. A group-ring multiplicity then appears, in analogy with the classical Hida-theory picture. So the ratio should exceed 1.

**Solution 2** claims the ratio is $r$. That is the linear growth one would expect from the oldform tower $f(z), f(\wp z), \dots$. But $U_\wp$ acts with nonzero eigenvalue only on a one-dimensional piece of that tower, so linear growth does not hold in the finite-slope setting. I see no support for it.

**Solution 3** claims $q^{2D(r-1)}$. Its reasoning is shaky and it second-guesses itself. It counts an extra factor from unipotent cosets, but $U_\wp$ already accounts for that part. By my own heuristic the answer should be $q^{D(r-1)}$, from the p-part of the diamond group alone. So its exponent looks off by a factor of 2. Of the three, it is the only one that has the right qualitative shape, a power of $q$ growing with $r$.

My recollection of Hattori's result is that the ratio is $q^{D(r-1)}$, but I am not certain of it, and none of the three solutions states that value. I choose Solution 3 as the closest, though it is probably wrong.

CHOICE: 3
